newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable, eyes on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable, eyes on rupiah.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices were stable in early trading on Monday, but most traders said they were cautious over the rupiah's movements.
They said traders offered rubber at 42.25 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for October shipment and at 42.50 for November shipment, but buyers were bidding at 41.50.
Offer prices were quoted at 42.00 fob Padang for October shipment, 41.25 fob Pontianak and 42.75 fob Medan.
"With the rupiah moving like this, both buyers and sellers are taking a wait-and-see position because they don't know what's going to happen next to the rupiah," said one Jakarta trader.

Rupiah was weak against the dollar in early trading on Monday but appeared to have stabilised, dealers said. Spot rupiah was at 2,935/40 at 0300 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,875/95. The early low was 2,950.
"I think prices will tend to decline further because of the fluctuations in the rupiah. Some traders anticipate prices to fall to as low as 40.00 (U.S. cents/lb)," one trader said.
"Those who have offered rubber are traders who are in need of cash. Otherwise, they just wait," he added.
Some traders said the drought had started to have an impact on supply. Others talked about the possibility of Thailand selling its excess stocks.
Regional traders said on Monday the fall in regional currencies and the prospect of Bangkok selling its excess rubber stocks would keep the market sentiment weak this week.
